q: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral and BC is a diameter of the related circle on which A and D also lie. ∠BCA = 19° and ∠CAD = 32°. What is the measure of ∠ACD?
solution:

Since ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, ∠BAD + ∠BCD = 180°.

∴ ∠BCD = 180° − 122° = 58°.

∠ACD = ∠BCD − ∠BCA = 58° − 19° = 39°.

∴ The correct answer is 39°.

Alternate Method

Formula Used: Angle in a semi-circle is 90°; Sum of opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral is 180°.

⇒ ∠BAD = ∠BAC + ∠CAD = 90° + 32° = 122°.

⇒ For cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, ∠BAD + ∠BCD = 180°.

⇒ 122° + ∠BCD = 180°.

⇒ ∠BCD = 180° − 122° = 58°.

⇒ We know ∠BCD = ∠BCA + ∠ACD.

⇒ 58° = 19° + ∠ACD.

⇒ ∠ACD = 58° − 19° = 39°.

∴ The correct answer is 39°.

q: PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral. If ∠P is three times of ∠R and ∠S is four times of ∠Q, then the sum of ∠S + ∠R will be:

∴ The correct answer is 189°.

∠S = 4 × ∠Q

Formula Used:

In a cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of opposite angles is 180°.

∠P + ∠R = 180°

∠Q + ∠S = 180°



Calculations:

Case 1: ∠P and ∠R are opposite angles.

⇒ ∠P + ∠R = 180°

⇒ 3∠R + ∠R = 180°

⇒ 4∠R = 180°

⇒ ∠R = 45°

Case 2: ∠S and ∠Q are opposite angles.

⇒ ∠S + ∠Q = 180°

⇒ ∠S + (∠S ÷ 4) = 180°

⇒ (5 × ∠S) ÷ 4 = 180°

⇒ 5∠S = 720°

⇒ ∠S = 144°

Now, finding the required sum:

⇒ Sum = ∠S + ∠R

⇒ Sum = 144° + 45°

⇒ Sum = 189°

∴ The correct answer is 189°.

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

A quadrilateral is called cyclic if all its four vertices lie on a circle. The sum of any pair of opposite angles is 180°.

Exterior Angle of Cyclic Quadrilateral

The exterior angle formed by extending one side of a cyclic quadrilateral is equal to the interior opposite angle.

⇒ Number of diagonals = [8 × (8 − 3)] ÷ 2

∴ The correct answer is 20.

q: In a ΔABC, if ∠A = 90°, AC = 5 cm, BC = 9 cm, and in ΔPQR, ∠P = 90°, PR = 3 cm, QR = 8 cm, then:
solution:
Shortcut Trick

Compare corresponding parts of right-angled ΔABC and ΔPQR.

In ΔABC: Hypotenuse BC = 9 cm and Side AC = 5 cm.

In ΔPQR: Hypotenuse QR = 8 cm and Side PR = 3 cm.

Congruence (RHS) requires Hypotenuse 1 = Hypotenuse 2 and Side 1 = Side 2.

Since 9 ≠ 8 and 5 ≠ 3, the triangles cannot be congruent.

∴ The correct answer is ΔABC ≇ ΔPQR.

Alternate Method

Given:

ΔABC: ∠A = 90°, AC = 5 cm, BC = 9 cm (Hypotenuse)

ΔPQR: ∠P = 90°, PR = 3 cm, QR = 8 cm (Hypotenuse)



Formula Used:

RHS (Right angle-Hypotenuse-Side) Congruence Rule: Two right-angled triangles are congruent if the hypotenuse and one side of one triangle are equal to the hypotenuse and the corresponding side of the other triangle.

⇒ In ΔABC, using Pythagoras theorem: AB² = BC² − AC²

⇒ AB² = 9² − 5² = 81 − 25 = 56
⇒ AB = √56 cm ≈ 7.48 cm

⇒ In ΔPQR, using Pythagoras theorem: PQ² = QR² − PR²

⇒ PQ² = 8² − 3² = 64 − 9 = 55
⇒ PQ = √55 cm ≈ 7.41 cm

⇒ Comparing the dimensions of ΔABC and ΔPQR:

⇒ Hypotenuse: BC (9 cm) ≠ QR (8 cm)
⇒ Side 1: AC (5 cm) ≠ PR (3 cm)
⇒ Side 2: AB (√56 cm) ≠ PQ (√55 cm)

⇒ Since none of the corresponding sides are equal, the triangles are not congruent.

∴ The correct answer is ΔABC ≇ ΔPQR.

Additional Information

RHS Congruence Rule

If in two right-angled triangles, the hypotenuse and one side of one triangle are equal to the hypotenuse and one side of the other triangle, then the two triangles are congruent.

SSS Congruence Rule

Two triangles are congruent if all three sides of one triangle are equal to the corresponding three sides of the other triangle.

Congruence vs. Equality

Congruent triangles (≅) have the exact same shape and size (identical sides and angles), whereas equal triangles (=) usually refers to triangles having equal area even if shapes differ.
